title: Molecular pixelation: spatial proteomics of single cells by sequencing
boundary: RCA-generated DNA pixels serially hybridize to antibody-oligo conjugates; gap-fill ligation installs two independent local-neighborhood identifiers before reporter PCR/NGS. Different physical capture/copying from one-RCA-tag PBA or transcript DNA microscopy, not merely more proteins.
evidence_scope: Published2024 primary Nature identity/abstract/workflow overview verified in indexed primary text; direct page later redirected to inaccessible identity endpoint. Whole Methods/SI not read, standard acquisition and comparison to actual PBA chemistry pending.

title: Spatially tunable multiomic sequencing using light-driven combinatorial barcoding of molecules in tissues
boundary: Photocaged-phosphate root oligos installed by RT or tagmentation; repeated ROI uncaging and overhang ligation writes combinatorial spatial digits with regenerated cages. Demonstrated RNA and chromatin-accessibility libraries, beyond one-shot LightSeq/PIC selection.
evidence_scope: Published PNAS2026 identity/abstract and Results barcoding overview verified in primary indexed article; primary PubMed42150070 confirms18May2026online/26Mayissue. No full Methods/SI or acquisition; preprint2024.05.20.595040 is same-work predecessor, not another candidate.

title: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics in fixed tissue using a cost-effective PCL-seq workflow
boundary: Photocleavable oligonucleotides and ligation adapters chemically label selected fixed-tissue ROIs for transcript-library readout; actual light-cleavage/ligation front end, not ordinary array pitch or tissue substitution. Compare full substrate/end chemistry to LightSeq/PSS/PHOTON before registration.
evidence_scope: Published Genome Research2025 title/DOI and abstract preparation overview verified in primary publisher PDF/index and PMC record40764053. Direct PMC original gated and later PubMed429; no repeated access or challenge bypass. Full Methods/SI acquisition pending.

title: Subcellular level spatial transcriptomics with PHOTON
boundary: RT primers carry N-POM-caged thymidines plus photocleavable blocked5prime phosphate; ROI illumination enables splinted PCR-handle ligation and biotin capture, then second-handle synthesis/NGS. RNA/dual-cage/splint preparation differs from genomic photoselection, not just better optics.
evidence_scope: Published14May2025 Nature primary identity and Results workflow/Fig1 overview read; page accessible. No complete source/SI pass, sequence transcription or molecular graph. Supersedes same-work preprint2024.09.10.612328; do not register both.

title: Photoselective sequencing: microscopically guided genomic measurements with subcellular resolution
boundary: An in-situ genomic/epigenomic fragment library is photocaged; targeted illumination chemically unmasks only selected spatial material for sequencer-library readout. Compare blocked-fragment/adaptor substrate to RNA RT-primer gates; not only image-guided dissection or computational localization.
evidence_scope: Published27April2023 Nature identity and primary abstract preparation boundary verified, plus PubMed37106232 abstract. Nature direct open redirected to inaccessible identity endpoint; indexed primary supplement overview names indexed P7 ligation adapters. No full Methods/SI or exact-end claim.

title: Profiling surface proteins on individual exosomes using a proximity barcoding assay
boundary: Antibody-DNA reporters on physically captured exosomes copy a shared complexTag from one RCA DNA bundle by polymerase extension, then PCR/NGS records protein/molecule/complex tags. Actual reporter-template transfer/capture chemistry differs from ordinary CITE tags and serial two-neighborhood gap-fill MPX.
evidence_scope: Published26August2019 Nature primary identity/abstract and Design and workflow/Fig1 overview verified; indexed primary complete page available, direct PMC gated. No full Methods/SI pass or source-oligo acquisition. Species/sample/panel applications remain one candidate.

title: Spatial reconstruction of immune niches by combining photoactivatable reporters and scRNA-seq
boundary: Two-photon activation of a genetically encoded fluorescent reporter labels a tissue niche; dissociation/FACS physically recovers selected cells before MARS-seq. Protein photoconversion/cell recovery differs from photocaged-dye SPACECAT or in-situ oligo/barcode activation.
evidence_scope: Published Science2017 identity verified by PubMed and author repository final PDF index; primary PMC7234837 preparation overview confirms PA-GFP/two-photon/FACS-to-MARS-seq. No full source/SI or downstream constructor inheritance; NicheNet software is not a candidate.
